analysis: The graph–SASRec ensemble achieved measured macro validation HR@10 of 0.595, improving on the reported graph score of 0.5388 by 0.0562 and baseline score of 0.505 by 0.0900. Category HR@10 was 0.650 for Movies_and_TV, 0.640 for Industrial_and_Scientific, 0.405 for Electronics, and 0.685 for CDs_and_Vinyl. These results support complementary ranking signals from graph structure and sequential behavior. Electronics remains the weakest category and did not exceed the previously reported SASRec score of 0.420, so fusion did not improve every category over its strongest known expert. Selected expert metrics are absent from the supplied host result, preventing attribution of gains to either expert or checkpoint selection. The successful trial consumed 1531.22 allocated GPU-seconds; no held-out test results were supplied.
code_summary: Each category independently trains a LightGCN expert and a causal SASRec expert sequentially on one GPU. LightGCN retains learned weights over three propagation depths, item biases, recency-weighted profiles with positive-target exclusion, and sampled-softmax training. SASRec uses a 50-item sequence, 50-dimensional embeddings, two attention blocks, one head, dropout 0.2, and pointwise BCE with unseen negatives. Each expert selects its checkpoint by validation HR@10, breaking ties with NDCG@10. Inference combines candidate ranks using equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion with constant 60 and item-ID tie-breaking. The exported predictor strictly reloads both experts, preserves complete graph histories and right-aligned SASRec histories, and routes all four datasets. Deterministic fixtures cover checkpoint reload, padding, empty histories, ties, candidate permutations, and predictor agreement.
